name: Methylstenbolone (M-Sten / Hybrid)
lead: Methylstenbolone (M-Sten, Methyl-Sten, Ultradrol) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid, the 17-alpha-methylated derivative of stenbolone. It was never introduced for medical use and has been sold online as a nutritional supplement.[1][2]
Published work consists mainly of metabolism and doping-detection studies, supplement analyses and a case report of cholestatic jaundice.[3][4][5][6]

paras: It is described as a 17-alpha-alkylated androstane with a 2-alpha-methyl group; the 17-alpha methylation is associated with oral activity and liver burden.[2]

No studies found of methylstenbolone in a clinical trial. A 2014 case report described cholestatic jaundice in a person using a supplement found to contain methylstenbolone and dymethazine.[6] A 2023 analysis examined androgenic steroids in over-the-counter supplements and adverse health effects.[8]

A 2013 study detected it in a supplement and described urinary metabolites; later work identified long-term metabolites for doping control, used human liver microsomes and a chimeric mouse model, and studied metabolism in horses.[3][4][5][7] Methylstenbolone is prohibited in sport.[7]

card.summary: An oral designer androgen sold as a supplement or research chemical; no trials, with a case report of cholestatic jaundice.
card.note: Prohibited in sport; liver injury case report.

quick.overview:
Methylstenbolone is an unapproved oral androgen sold online in muscle-building supplements.

Research is mostly about detecting and metabolising it, plus a few case reports.
quick.mechanism: It is classed as an androgen receptor agonist; 17-alpha methylation is associated with oral activity.
quick.risks: A case report links a product containing it to cholestatic jaundice. It is prohibited in sport and has no approved medical use.
